title: Climate-risk ZIP codes show higher homeowners-insurance cost and nonrenewal exposure
source_unit: Treasury Federal Insurance Office analysis of aggregated homeowners-insurance policy and ZIP-code data
geography: United States; ZIP codes grouped by expected annual building losses from nine climate-related perils

observations.period: 2018-2022; highest versus lowest climate-risk ZIP-code quintiles

denominator.unit: published ZIP-code risk-quintile comparison; policy-level premium averages

high_risk_average_premium_per_policy.unit: 2022 dollars per policy, average for highest-risk ZIP quintile

high_risk_premium_difference.unit: percent higher than lowest-risk ZIP quintile

observations.method: Treasury FIO analysis of NAIC/state-regulator data from more than 330 insurers and over 246 million policies, grouped by expected annual losses to buildings from nine climate-related perils.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports a risk-group comparison, not a causal decomposition of climate risk, reconstruction costs, inflation, reinsurance, regulation, insurer mix, or property composition.
observations.subgroup: ZIP codes in the highest and lowest 20 percent of expected annual building losses; ZIP-level groups are not household income groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher premiums may reflect several correlated risks and costs; the result does not show that a particular household received a quote or could not obtain coverage.

observations.period: 2018-2022; highest versus lowest climate-risk ZIP-code quintiles

denominator.unit: published ZIP-code risk-quintile comparison; policy nonrenewal rates

high_risk_nonrenewal_difference.unit: percent higher average nonrenewal rate than lowest-risk ZIP quintile, approximate

observations.method: Treasury FIO comparison of reported policy nonrenewal and paid-claim metrics across climate-risk ZIP-code groups.
observations.uncertainty: Nonrenewal is an insurer-policy event, not a direct household availability or relocation measure; claim severity averages do not identify claim type, household loss, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: Highest and lowest climate-risk ZIP-code quintiles.
observations.counterinterpretation: Nonrenewals may reflect underwriting, property condition, policy mix, or state rules as well as expected climate loss; higher claim severity may reflect different insured assets.

denominator.unit: ZIP-code-year rows with at least 10 reporting insurers and 50 policies; workbook includes 2018-2022

available_metrics.value: claim frequency; claim severity; loss ratio; premiums per policy; nonrenewal rate; nonpayment cancellation rate; other-than-nonpayment cancellation rate

coverage.unit: percent of HO-3 and HO-5 policies nationwide measured by direct premiums written, as described by Treasury

observations.method: Treasury-released aggregated ZIP-code/year workbook underlying the FIO analysis; data are not a complete census of insurers, forms, residual markets, E&S markets, flood insurance, or 2023-2024 activity.
observations.uncertainty: Treasury warns of variable state and ZIP-code scope, retrospective reporting inconsistencies, anomalies, and limited representativeness where smaller insurers were not asked to report. The workbook is suitable for aggregate analysis more than individual ZIP inference.
observations.subgroup: Qualifying ZIP-code/year observations, with policy-count decile and climate-risk group fields available in the workbook.
observations.counterinterpretation: Observed market metrics cannot by themselves connect insurer decisions to household income, coverage adequacy, repairs, mortgage access, moves, or political response.

related_sources.claim: The FIO annual report supplies the detailed methodology and market context for the release and workbook.
related_sources.access_boundary: The public data window ends in 2022 and does not establish 2023-2025 market conditions.

related_sources.claim: The local reproducible audit counts valid rows by year and documents that policy-count deciles are distinct from climate-risk groups.
related_sources.access_boundary: The audit checks workbook structure and completeness; it does not validate the underlying insurer submissions.

boundary: This record establishes a market-side association between climate-risk ZIP-code groupings and reported premiums, nonrenewals, and claim severity in 2018-2022. It does not establish household-level affordability, actual coverage loss, repair or move outcomes, causation, or political/geopolitical consequence. Those links remain open for matched place-time work.
